bib.title: Energy and Policy Considerations for Deep Learning in NLP
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), pages 3645-3650

question: What are the financial and carbon costs of training and developing recent NLP neural models, and what should the community do about them?
contributions: Estimate energy, CO2 and cloud cost of training BERT, ELMo, Transformer, GPT-2 and NAS from reported training times
Case study of total compute to develop LISA, including all tuning
Recommendations: report training time and hyperparameter sensitivity; equitable compute access; efficient hardware and algorithms

method.summary: Power draw is sampled while training each model with default code for up to 1 day; total training time is taken from the original papers and converted to kWh with PUE 1.58, then to CO2e with the US EPA factor, and to dollars with cloud prices. A case study sums the logs of all jobs behind LISA.
method.task: energy, carbon and dollar cost estimation of NLP model training

datasets.name: LISA project training logs (Strubell et al. 2018)

other.steps: 979M training steps in total; base model 10 h per 300k steps on one TPUv2 core

inference.samples: one power-sampling run per model, max 1 day each; no repeats stated

parameters.measurement_hardware: single NVIDIA Titan X; ELMo on 3 GTX 1080 Ti; nvidia-smi for GPU, Intel RAPL for CPU/DRAM

baselines: familiar consumption: air travel, human life, car lifetime (Table 1)
eval.protocol: estimates, no repeated measurement or error bars

availability.code: models' public code used out-of-the-box; no code released for estimates

evidence.quote: We use a PUE coefﬁcient of 1.58

results.setup: Estimated from training times and hardware reported in the original papers, power sampled on a single Titan X (ELMo: 3 GTX 1080 Ti) with default code, PUE 1.58, US EPA 0.954 lbs CO2/kWh; NAS from So et al. 2019, 274,120 hours on 8 P100

results.table: Table 3, row NAS P100x8, column CO2e

results.claim: Developing one NLP model (LISA) took 4789 jobs across 123 grid searches over 172 days.
results.setup: Strubell et al. 2018 project logs; Titan X 72%, M40 28%

results.claim: Total GPU time for the LISA project was 9998 days (27 years), about 60 GPUs running constantly for 6 months.
Full R&D for LISA cost $103k-$350k in cloud compute and $9870 in electricity (239,942 hours).

Training one NLP pipeline (parsing, SRL) emits 39 lbs CO2e, 78,468 with tuning and experiments.
Owning 8x1080 Ti servers for the case study (about 58 GPUs, 172 days) would cost $145,000 plus electricity, about half on-demand cloud.

limits: Power measured on Titan X / 1080 Ti GPUs but applied to training times from papers that used P100, V100 or TPUs; per-model power is an approximation.
TPU power and carbon are omitted for lack of public data.
CO2 uses the US average grid; cloud providers differ (Table 2).
Single-day power sampling, no repeats or uncertainty.
Numbers are 2019 hardware and prices; cloud prices and efficiency have changed.
Only one development case study (LISA); NAS and GPT-2 dev costs are not logged.
GPT-2 hardware and time came from the authors on Reddit.

terms.definition: Power Usage Effectiveness, accounts for the additional energy required to support the compute infrastructure (mainly cooling)
